extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in journalism/media ethics (journalists, editors, media-watchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A short news item reporting a specific incident of a newspaper photographer altering an image and the newsroom's response; highlights ethics and disciplinary consequences for photo manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulating published photographs / maintain image authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: In Patrick Schneider’s original photo, the sky was brownish-gray. He manipulated the image and the sky became a deep red and the sun took on a more distinct halo, says Observer editor Rick Thames. Schneider, who was suspended in 2003 for tweaking colors in photos, has been fired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Altering the visual content of news photographs (e.g., changing sky color or adding halos) breaches newsroom standards of authenticity and can result in suspension or termination, as illustrated by this reporter’s 2003 suspension for color tweaks and subsequent firing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and enforcement of photo standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Observer editor Rick Thames identified the manipulation and the newsroom took disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are expected to detect and respond to image manipulation; active oversight and enforcement (investigation, suspension, firing) are part of upholding photographic integrity in newsrooms.
